findings.text: _read_crew_plan_details re-implements the 16384-byte head slice and </head> split and calls the un-memoised read_state, then falls back to parse_meta, leaving two parse routes for one plan file even though an outer memoized(...) wrapper now caches the result per stat.

the latency assertion is a wall-clock bound (elapsed < 1.0 s) measured on a shared node; head 0.223 s against base 2.041 s leaves a wide margin, but a loaded host could redden it without a regression.

item_verdicts.diff: read against base f31a38d86: af7577adc short-circuits the recorded phase, a5c209881 populates the latency fixture, 0185df065 reads roster headers and plan head, 43f21cb99 memoises plan navigation, 0005242af requires headers_only on both loaders, the docs commits register the landing, and the fragment's evidence-commit tracks the measured source revision.
item_verdicts.done_when: verified: tests/test_a_launched_run_reads_launching_on_crew.py:93 writes a pointer with phase=starting and no stream file and asserts the first /crew response carries a launch-phase row, and :107 populates 40 live pointers (streams absent for run-00) and asserts elapsed < 1.0 s. I reproduced the focused file at reviewed head d988b162 against the reviewed worktree: 3 passed EXIT=0.
item_verdicts.goal: verified: the delta carries both halves of section 3's done-when. reckon/serve.py:753 short-circuits a recorded phase past launch so a run whose worker has not written a stream reads launching or working from the first response, and the latency work (header-only roster read, tail only for unresolved phases, memoised plan navigation) brings GET /crew over 40 live pointers to 0.223 s, against 2.041 s at base. The one point withheld is that the first-response test accepts {'launching','starting','working'} (tests/test_a_launched_run_reads_launching_on_crew.py:103), marginally looser than the done-when's literal launching-or-working.
item_verdicts.manifest: read: status complete, eight commits, a clean tree checkpoint, the negative control, the focused gate and the serve-importing population; baseline_suite (baseline-suite.log, revision f31a38d86, 5 failures) and after_suite (granted-after-suite.log, revision 0005242af, 0 failures) are both present and completed, so the added-failure count reads as a measured zero.
item_verdicts.write_paths: verified: git diff --stat f31a38d86..d988b162c6 names reckon/serve.py, tests/test_a_launched_run_reads_launching_on_crew.py, tests/test_crew_route_cost.py and the evidence fragment; all four sit inside the manifest's declared write grants, tests/test_crew_route_cost.py having been recorded there as a granted scope extension.

justifications.durability: Each half is guarded: the first-response assertion fails with 'idle' when the phase derives from the stream alone (negative control), and the timing assertion fails at 2.041 s when full classification is reinstated (base arm); the new plan-navigation test guards the memoisation's invalidation on a plan-file change. One point withheld: the latency gate is a wall-clock bound (<1.0 s) on a shared node -- a wide margin at 0.223 s, but a loaded host could redden it without a regression.
justifications.evidence: I reproduced the focused gate at reviewed head myself (3 passed EXIT=0), the declared negative control is a real red log (EXIT=1, test_first_response_shows_a_dispatched_run_without_a_stream fails with 'idle'), and the base timing arm fails at 2.041 s where the head passes at 0.223 s. Both population arms are present and honest: base 5 failures (1 failed + 4 errors, all test_build, attributed to the scratch tree lacking Git metadata), after 0 failures, so the added-failure count is a measured zero.
justifications.fit: The change extends the existing _crew_rows owner and reads the same classify_pointer judgement; the previous review's two follow-ons are addressed, the unreachable TypeError fallback is gone (headers_only passed directly) and plan navigation is memoised. One point withheld: _read_crew_plan_details still re-implements a 16384-byte head slice plus read_state rather than composing _plan_html's own fast path, leaving two parse routes for one plan file.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The two halves of section 3's done-when are both implemented and both pinned: a no-stream dispatch reads launching/working from the first response, and the 40-pointer fixture answers in 0.223 s against 2.041 s at base. One point withheld: the first-response assertion permits 'starting' as well as launching/working, a hair looser than the done-when's wording.
